lowerBound.description: The lower bound of this comparator set. For example `3.0.0-0` in `>=3.0.0-0 <4.0.0-0`.

upperBound.description: The upper bound of this comparator set. For example `4.0.0-0` in `>=3.0.0-0 <4.0.0-0`.

lowerInclusive.description:
False if {@link #lowerBound} uses {@link SemanticVersionRange.Operation#GT}.

True if {@link #lowerBound} uses {@link SemanticVersionRange.Operation#GTE}.

Example:
- `>3.0.0 <=4.0.0` -> `false`
- `>=3.0.0-0 <4.0.0-0` -> `true`

upperInclusive.description:
False if {@link #lowerBound} uses {@link SemanticVersionRange.Operation#LT}.

True if {@link #lowerBound} uses {@link SemanticVersionRange.Operation#LTE}.

Example:
- `>=3.0.0-0 <4.0.0-0` -> `false`
- `>3.0.0 <=4.0.0` -> `true`

title:
Representation of a comparator set as defined in {@link SemanticVersionRange}.
Comparator sets are always represented as a pair of comparators so that version ranges are always represented in
their simplest form.

For example, `>3 <5 <4` is no different than `>3 < 4`.
name: SemanticVersionRange.Requirement
